channels.title: Add other channels
channels.description: This recorder has {count} other channels with a camera on them. Add all of them, or tick the ones you want. Channels that are empty, switched off, or reached over ONVIF are not listed, because this integration cannot drive them.

areas.title: Where are these cameras?
areas.description: Pick an area for each one and they will be filed as they are added. Leave any of them blank to decide later. New areas can be created here if you need them.

reconfigure.title: Dahua Camera Connection
reconfigure.description: Update how Home Assistant reaches this device. Credentials are unchanged; use re-authentication for those.

data.channel: Channel (a single camera is 0. On an NVR this is the 0-based index, which is one less than the number the recorder shows: its channel 4 is 3 here)
data.use_https: Use HTTPS (otherwise HTTPS is used only on port 443)

progress.discover: Looking for other channels on this device. This can take up to {seconds} seconds.

error.auth: The camera rejected that username and password.
error.channel_not_on_device: The recorder does not have that channel. This field counts from 0, so the recorder's channel 4 is 3 here and its last channel is one less than the number it shows.
error.channel_disabled: That channel exists on the recorder but is switched off, so it has no camera to read. Enable it on the recorder first, then add it here.
error.channel_is_onvif: That channel is reached over ONVIF, which this integration cannot drive: the recorder does not serve it on its own Dahua paths. Use Home Assistant's ONVIF integration for that camera, or switch the channel to Dahua's own protocol on the recorder.
error.cannot_connect: Nothing answered at that address and port. Check the camera is on, that the IP and port are right, and that Home Assistant can reach it.
error.timeout: The camera did not answer in time. It may be busy, or reachable but very slow — try again, and check the port is the one it serves HTTP on.
error.ssl_error: The secure connection failed. If the camera does not serve HTTPS, clear the HTTPS option; if it does, it is usually on port 443.
error.unexpected_reply: Something answered, but not a Dahua camera. Check the port — the web interface and the API are not always the same one.
error.cgi_disabled: That address is serving web pages, but not the Dahua API. On a Dahua device this is almost always the CGI service being switched off: turn it on under System, then Security or Safety, then System Service, then CGI, and try again. If CGI is already on, check the port, because the web interface and the API are not always the same one.
error.https_available: Nothing answered on that port, but the device is listening on 443, so it is probably serving HTTPS. Tick the HTTPS option and use port 443.
error.http_service_off: The device is switched on and answering Dahua's own protocol, but nothing is serving HTTP on that port, so the integration cannot reach its API. Its web service is most likely switched off: turn on HTTP and CGI under System, then Security or Safety, then System Service.
error.unknown: Could not add the camera. The Home Assistant log has the reason.

abort.single_instance_allowed: Only a single instance is allowed.
abort.already_configured: Only a single instance of a device is allowed.

data.auto_detect_channel: Auto-detect channel index (disable if HTTP snapshot at channel=0 works but RTSP only streams on channel=1)
data.use_rpc2: Read configuration over one RPC2 session per device (fewer logins in the device's log; leave off if unsure)
data.scan_interval: Seconds between device polls (events are not affected)
data.disable_backchannel: Don't open the two-way audio channel when streaming (fixes a doorbell stuck in a call, or talkback in the Dahua/Amcrest app; disables talking from Home Assistant)
data.authorized_plates: Authorized license plates (comma-separated, e.g. ABC1234, XYZ5678)
data.authorized_hold_time: Authorized vehicle hold time (seconds to remain ON)

data_description.manual_siren: Enable this if your camera has a working siren, but the integration did not create the Siren entity.
data_description.manual_security_light: Enable this if your camera has a working security light, but the integration did not create the Security Light entity.

removal_broke_things.title: {dependents} referenced the Dahua entry you removed
removal_broke_things.description:
You removed **{removed}**, and {dependents} referred to entities it provided:

{names}

Those entities no longer exist, so anything using them stops working quietly rather than reporting an error. Worth checking each one.

This is only a notice -- dismiss it once you have looked.

device_unreachable.title: Dahua device at {address} is not responding
device_unreachable.description:
Home Assistant has not been able to reach the Dahua device at {address} for about {minutes} minutes. {entries} configuration entries use this device.

Check that it is powered on and reachable on your network. The debugging section of the documentation explains how to capture logs.

This message disappears on its own as soon as the device answers again.

http_dead_https_available.title: Dahua device at {address} answers on HTTPS but not on port {port}

confirm.title: Switch {address} to HTTPS
confirm.description:
The Dahua device at {address} has stopped answering on port {port}, but it accepts connections on port 443. Some Dahua firmwares stop serving plain HTTP while HTTPS keeps working.

This changes the {entries} Dahua configuration entries for {address} to port 443 with HTTPS, reloading them one at a time.

Your username and password are not changed.
